definition: Estimates Pandemic Early-Warning Nets readiness from component maturity.

title: Pandemic Early-Warning Nets Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Pandemic Early-Warning Nets operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Pandemic Early-Warning Nets installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 85253 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where sensor grids monitoring, net logistics redundancy, or genomic surveillance maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Pandemic Early-Warning Nets Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Pandemic Early-Warning Nets: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Pandemic Early-Warning Nets — nets detecting outbreaks before they spread.

Phase 1 — Prove (sensor grids): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (net logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (genomic surveillance): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (alert protocols): net hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and public health-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
